title: Laredo’s PILLAR Keeps Free HIV Testing Going Despite Funding Concerns
excerpt: PILLAR continues to offer free, confidential HIV testing in Laredo despite federal funding concerns, along with support groups and emergency help with medication, housing, food and utilities.
content:
PILLAR continues to offer free HIV testing in Laredo despite federal funding concerns, according to KGNS. PILLAR stands for People with Ideas of Love, Liberty, Acceptance and Respect.

Testing is free and confidential and open to anyone in the community, with walk-ins welcome, whether or not they are part of the LGBTQ+ community. Staff encourage testing even for people who feel healthy.

PILLAR also offers support groups, transportation to medical appointments, and emergency assistance for medication, housing, food and utilities.

More than 200,000 people in the United States are unaware they have HIV, and there are more than 5,000 new HIV diagnoses in Texas each year, according to figures cited in the report.

PILLAR is at 2007 San Bernardo Ave. in Laredo. Its hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed noon to 1 p.m. for lunch, and its phone number is (956) 725-0066.

A World AIDS Day event is scheduled for Dec. 1, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at PILLAR, with free testing, food, music, prizes and information.

Source: KGNS, Nov. 17, 2026.
